prompt:
A desktop marketing landing page for White Sail Labs, an independent market research lab, rendered edge to edge at 1440 by 900 with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it.

The visitor is an investor, CEO or strategist deciding whether to request early access. White Sail Labs sells research as a subscription: applied AI engineers and business engineers build an always-on fleet of agents that keeps a living world model of every company. When a new fact arrives, only the surprise, the part the model did not expect, travels along the value chain, link by link.

The page IS a synoptic pressure chart of the economy, filling the viewport edge to edge, fine navy isobar lines sweeping behind everything. A deep navy band across the top carries a cream sail silhouette with three short speed lines beside the wordmark White Sail Labs, and the navigation Who we are, Capabilities, Careers, Contact, Request early access.

What leads is one numbered ripple through the world model, flowing left to right across the upper two thirds, tagged Illustrative. Step 1, a solid station at far left: "SK hynix · Supplier · HBM output guidance +20% · model expected +12% · surprise +8 pts". Step 2, a thick gold front with semicircles carries only that surprise to a larger station in the centre: "NVIDIA · GPU shipments forecast +3.2%", the link labelled "elasticity 0.4". Step 3, thinner gold fronts continue to two customer stations at right: "Microsoft · AI capacity forecast +1.1%" and "Meta · capex forecast +0.9%". Step 4, a thin navy front with triangles branches down and right to a competitor: "Samsung · HBM share forecast −0.6 pts". The fronts get thinner as the surprise travels; the reported fact is set in solid type, every forecast in light hairline type.

The chart's title block, a ruled rectangle inset in the lower left corner, holds the headline "Your decisions. Better informed." set very large, the line "A research lab of people and agents, not an AI tool.", and the actions Request early access and Get in touch. The bottom margin reads "Issued 11 Nov 09:42 · Next update: continuous".

Visual law: a met office chart's crisp off-white ground, deep navy and warm gold as the only two inks, no red anywhere, station plots and front symbols as the signature, labels in a clear technical grotesk. One dominant move: the numbered ripple.
approval_note: Approved in the comp round as option one. Carry over the Who we are key strip from option two (further down the page) and option three's step-by-step visual as a pinned scroll section, not the first viewport, on a different example such as an oil shock rippling through fuel into logistics.
